It provides:\n5\t\n6\t- Device management and GPU selection policies\n7\t- Persistent array base types and allocation conventions\n8\t- Module stability markers for JIT compilation\n9\t- Capture-safe stepping protocol\n10\t- Profiling hooks and instrumentation\n11\t\n12\tDesign Principles\n13\t----------------\n14\t1. **Module stability before JIT churn**: All kernels in a module compile together.\n15\t   Stabilize module contents early to avoid reload churn.\n16\t2. **Persistent arrays over temporaries**: Field buffers are allocated once and\n17\t   reused across timesteps to minimize allocation overhead.\n18\t3. **Capture-safe stepping**: Kernels must not capture mutable state from the\n19\t   outer Python scope. All timestep-dependent values must be passed as arguments.\n20\t4. **Explicit device placement**: Arrays carry device affinity explicitly rather\n21\t   than relying on global state.\n22\t5. **Structured profiling**: Use Warp's ScopedTimer and NVTX markers for\n23\t   GPU-side instrumentation, with CPU-side timing hooks for end-to-end metrics.\n24\t\n25\tDevice Management\n26\t-----------------\n27\t- Use ``get_warp_device()`` to obtain the default device or a specific GPU.\n28\t- For multi-GPU: map logical chunk indices to device IDs via\n29\t  ``ChunkLayout.device_assignment``.\n30\t- All array allocations use the target device explicitly.\n31\t\n32\tArray Conventions\n33\t----------------\n34\t- Field arrays: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.float32 or wp.complex64, shape=(Nx, Ny, Nz, 3))``\n35\t- Coefficient arrays: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.float32, shape=(Nx, Ny, Nz))``\n36\t- Auxiliary state: ``wp.array(dtype=wp.complex64, shape=(num_poles, Nx, Ny, Nz))``\n37\t- All arrays are allocated on the target device; no managed memory unless explicit.\n38\t\n39\tDtype Policy\n40\t-----------\n41\t- Single precision (float32/complex64) is the default for GPU execution.\n42\t- Double precision (float64/complex128) is available but may significantly\n43\t  reduce performance on consumer NVIDIA GPUs.\n44\t- Complex fields are required when any Bloch boundary is present.\n45\t- The ``requires_complex_fields`` flag from ``BoundarySpecIR`` determines whether\n46\t  to use complex dtype for field storage.\n47\t\n48\tModule Stability\n49\t---------------\n50\tUse ``mark_module_stable()`` after defining all kernels in a module.\n51\tThis signals that the module's kernel set is frozen and ready for JIT.\n52\tDuring development, unstable modules trigger a warning on import.\n53\t\n54\tCapture-Safe Stepping\n55\t---------------------\n56\tEvery kernel function that depends on timestep-varying values (dt, time, step_index)\n57\tmust receive those values as explicit arguments. Do NOT capture them from closure.\n58\t\n59\tExample::\n60\t\n61\t    # BAD - captures dt from outer scope\n62\t    @wp.kernel\n63\t    def bad_update(E, H,):\n64\t        dt = outer_dt  # captured!\n65\t        ...\n66\t\n67\t    # GOOD - dt passed explicitly\n68\t    @wp.kernel\n69\t    def good_update(E, H, dt: float):\n70\t        ...\n71\t\n72\tCapture-safe stepping also means:\n73\t- Source amplitudes are computed outside the kernel and passed as arrays or scalars\n74\t- Monitor intervals are evaluated in Python before calling recording kernels\n75\t- Boundary coefficients are pre-compiled and passed as array arguments\n76\t\n77\tProfiling Hooks\n78\t---------------\n79\t- ``WarpTimer`` context manager for GPU-side kernel timing\n80\t- ``nvtx_range`` for annotating execution phases\n81\t- ``step_metrics()`` helper for computing cells/s and Gcells/s\n82\t\n83\tReferences\n84\t----------\n85\t- Warp docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/warp-py\n86\t- GPU Benchmarking: ``../papers/gpu_benchmarking.pdf``\n87\t- Chunk Contract: ``../phase1/architecture/chunk-contract.md``\n88\t\"\"\"\n89\t\n90\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n91\t\n92\tfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n93\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n94\tfrom typing import Any, Literal\n95\t\n96\t__all__ = [\n97\t    \"WARP_AVAILABLE\",\n98\t    \"wp\",\n99\t    \"get_warp_device\",\n100\t    \"get_default_device\",\n101\t    \"allocate_field_array\",\n102\t    \"allocate_coefficient_array\",\n103\t    \"allocate_auxiliary_array\",\n104\t    \"FieldArrayTag\",\n105\t    \"CoefficientArrayTag\",\n106\t    \"AuxiliaryArrayTag\",\n107\t    \"ArrayTags\",\n108\t    \"WarpTimer\",\n109\t    \"nvtx_range\",\n110\t    \"step_metrics\",\n111\t    \"backend_info\",\n112\t    \"WarpBackendInfo\",\n113\t    \"ComplexFieldPolicy\",\n114\t    \"ModuleStability\",\n115\t    \"mark_module_stable\",\n116\t    \"is_module_stable\",\n117\t]\n118\t\n119\t\n120\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n121\t# Warp import with graceful fallback\n122\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n123\t\n124\ttry:\n125\t    import warp as wp\n126\texcept ModuleNotFoundError:  # kernels\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    @wp.kernel\n    def pole_residue_electric_update_3d(\n        E: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n        H: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n        e_decay_xx: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n        e_decay_yy: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n        e_decay_zz: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n        e_drive_xx:        nx, ny, nz: Grid dimensions.\n        \"\"\"\n        i, j, k = wp.tid()\n\n        if i < 1 or i >= nx - 1 or j < 1 or j >= ny - 1 or k < 1 or k >= nz - 1:\n            return\n\n polarization current\n        for p_idx in range(num_poles):\n            # p_drive for each field component (same for all components since\n            # we use the scalar E field value for the -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Apply a compiled mode source to the supplied field buffers.\n\n    ModeSource uses the equivalence principle: tangential E and H field\n    components from the mode profile are converted to J and M currents.\n    For direction=\"+\", H fields contribute to E injection and E fields\n    contribute to H injection (forward propagation). magnetic_np.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\"electric_field and magnetic_field must have matching shapes\")\n    if electric_np.ndim != 4 or electric_np.shape[-1] != 3:\n        raise ValueError(\"field arrays must have shape (nx, ny, nz, 3)\")\n\n    amplitude = compiled_source.amplitude_at_time(time) * dt\n    updated_electric = electric_np.astype(np.result_type(electric_np.dtype, np.complex128), copy=True)\n    updated_magnetic = magnetic_np.astype(np.result_type(magnetic_np.dtype, np.complex128), copy=True)\n\n    direction_sign = 1.0 if compiled_source.direction == \"+\" else -1.0\n    injection_axis = compiled_source.injection_axis\n\n    e_data = compiled_source.e_field_data\n    h_data = compiled_source.h_field_data\n\n    tang_axes = tuple(a for a in range(3) if a != injection_axis)\n    tang_axis_a, tang_axis_b = tang_axes\n\n    power_norm = 1.0 / math.sqrt(compiled_source.mode_power) if compiled_source.mode_power > 0 else 1.0\n\n    for placement, weight in zip(\n        compiled_source.placements,\n        compiled_source.placement_weights,\n        strict=True,\n    ):\n        idx_x, idx_y = placement[tang_axis_a], placement[tang_axis_b]\n\n        ex_val = e_data[\"Ex\"][idx_x, idx_y] if \"Ex\" in e_data else 0.0\n        ey_val = e_data[\"Ey\"][idx_x, idx_y] if \"Ey\" in e_data else 0.0\n        hx_val = h_data[\"Hx\"][idx_x, idx_y] if \"Hx\" in h_data else 0.0\n        hy_val = h_data[\"Hy\"][idx_x, idx_y] if \"Hy\" in h_data else 0.0\n\n        if direction_sign > 0:\n            updated_electric[placement][tang_axis_a] += amplitude * weight * power_norm * (-hy_val)\n            updated_electric[placement][tang_axis_b] += updated_electric[placement][tang_axis_b] += amplitude * weight * power_norm * (-hx_val)\n            updated_magnetic[placement][tang_axis_a] += amplitude * weight * power_norm * (-ey_val)\n wp.array(data=updated_magnetic, dtype=wp.float32, device=dev)\n        return new_E, new_H\n\n    return updated_electric, updated_magnetic\n\n\ndef inject_plane_wave(\n    electric_field,\n    magnetic_field,\n    compiled_source: CompiledPlaneWave,\n    *,\n    time: float,\n    dt: float = 1.0,\n    freq: float | None = None,\n) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Apply a compiled plane wave source to the supplied field buffers.\n\n    A PlaneWave injects a spatially uniform electromagnetic wave with a defined\n    propagation direction and polarization. The source uses the equivalence\n    principle: J = n × H and M = -n × E, where n is the source normal.\n\n    When given a wp.array, preserves device array.\n    \"\"\"\n    if dt <= 0.0:\n        raise ValueError(\"dt must be positive\")\n\n    is_warp = _is_warp_array(electric_field)\n    if is_warp:\n        dev = electric_field.device\n        electric_np = electric_field.numpy()\n updated_magnetic[placement][tang_axis_b] += e_tang_a * direction_sign\n        else:\n            updated_magnetic[placement][tang_axis_a] += (-e_tang_b) * direction_sign\n            updated_magnetic[placement][tang_axis_b] += e_tang_a * direction_sign\n            updated_electric[placement][tang_axis_a] += (-h_tang_b) * direction_sign\n            updated_electric[placement][tang_axis_b] += h_tang_a * direction_sign\n\n    if is_warp:\n        new_E = wp.array(data=updated_electric, dtype=wp.float32, device=dev)\n        new_H = test_vacuum_propagation_is_energy_conserving(self):\n        \"\"\"Vacuum propagation should approximately conserve total energy.\"\"\"\n        # Initialize a plane wave pulse\n        cx, cy, cz = self.nx // 2, self.ny // 2, self.nz // 2\n\n        # Set a Gaussian pulse in Ez\n        sigma = 3\n        for i in range(self.nx):\n            for j in range(self.ny):\n                for k in range(self.nz):\n                    r2 = ((i - cx) ** 2 + (j - cy) ** 2 + (k - cz) ** 2) / (\n                        2 * sigma**2\n                    )\n                    self.arrays[\"E\"][i, j, k, 2] = np.exp(-r2)  # Ez component\n\n        # Record initial energy\n        i1, i2 = 1, self.nx - 1\n        j1, j2 = 1, self.ny - 1\n        k1, k2 = 1, self.nz - 1\n\n        E0_sq = np.sum(self.arrays[\"E\"][i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, :] ** 2)\n        H0_sq = np.sum(self.arrays[\"H\"][i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, :] ** 2)\n        initial_energy = 0.5 * (E0_sq + H0_sq)\n\n        # Run several steps\n        for step in range(50):\n            step_maxwell(\n                self.arrays,\n                self.dt,\n                self.dx,\n                self.dy,\n                self.dz,\n                step_index=step,\n                time=step * self.dt,\n            )\n\n        # Compute final energy\n        Ef_sq = np.sum(self.arrays[\"E\"][i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, :] ** 2)\n        Hf_sq = np.sum(self.arrays[\"H\"][i1:i2, j1:j2, k1:k2, :] ** 2)\n        final_energy = 0.5 * (Ef_sq + Hf_sq)\n\n        # Energy should be approximately conserved (within ~10% for this coarse test)\n        if initial_energy > 1e-10:\n            relative_change = abs(final_energy - initial_energy) / initial_energy\n            assert relative_change < 0.15, (\n                f\"Energy changed by {relative_change*100:.1f}%, \"\n                f\"expected < 15% for vacuum propagation\"\n            )\n\n    def test_vacuum_wave_propagates(self):\n        \"\"\"A field       Each component update uses neighbor E values at offset positions\n        corresponding to the Yee cell staggering.\n\n        Args:\n            H: Magnetic field array with shape (nx, ny, nz, 3), component order (Hx, Hy, Hz)\n            E: Electric field array with shape (nx, ny, nz, 3), component order (Ex, Ey, Ez)\n            mu_xx, mu_yy, mu_zz: Permeability arrays with shape (nx, ny, nz)\n            dt: Timestep size\n            dx, dy, dz: Cell sizes\n            nx, ny, nz: Grid dimensions\n        \"\"\"\n        i, j, k = wp.tid()\n\n        # Bounds check - update interior cells only (skip ghost cells at boundaries)\n        if i < 1 or i >= nx - 1 or j < 1 or j >= ny - 1 or k < 1 or k >= nz - 1:\n            return\n\n        # ---- Hx component update ----\n        # Hx at (i, j, k) uses Ey at (i, j, k) and (i, j, k+1) for dEy/dz\n        # and Ez at (i, j, k) and (i, j+1, k) for dEz/dy\n        # Hx_update = -dt/mu * (dEy_dz - dEz_dy)\n        Ey_at_ijk_Hx = E[i, j, k, _EY]\n        Ey_at_ijkp1 = E[i, j, k + 1, _EY]\n        Ez_at_ijk_Hx = E[i, j, k, _EZ]\n        Ez_at_ijp1k = E[i, j + 1, k, _EZ]\n\n        dEy_dz_Hx = (Ey_at_ijkp1 - Ey_at_ijk_Hx) / dz\n        dEz_dy_Hx = (Ez_at_ijp1k - Ez_at_ijk_Hx) / dy\n\n        mu_Hx = mu_xx[i, j, k]\n        ch_Hx = -dt / (mu_Hx + 1e-20)\n        H[i, j, k, _HX] += ch_Hx * (dEy_dz_Hx - dEz_dy_Hx)\n\n        # ---- Hy component update ----\n        # Hy at (i, j, k) uses Ez at (i, j, k) and (i+1, j, k) for dEz/dx\n        # and Ex at (i, j, k) and (i, j, k+1) for dEx/dz\n        Ez_at_ijk_Hy = E[i, j, k, _EZ]\n        Ez_at_ip1jk = E[i + 1, j, k, _EZ]\n        Ex_at_ijk_Hy = E[i, j, k, _EX]\n        Ex_at_ijkp1 = E[i, j, k + 1, _EX]\n\n        dEz_dx_Hy = (Ez_at_ip1jk - Ez_at_ijk_Hy) / dx\n        dEx_dz_Hy = (Ex_at_ijkp1 - Ex_at_ijk_Hy) / dz\n\n        mu_Hy = mu_yy[i, j, k]\n        ch_Hy = -dt / (mu_Hy + 1e-20)\n        H[i, j, k, _HY] += ch_Hy * (dEz_dx_Hy - dEx_dz_Hy)\n\n        # ---- Hz component update ----\n        # Hz at (i, j, k) uses Ex at (i, j, k) and (i, j+1, k) for dEx/dy\n        # and Ey at (i, j, k) and (i+1, j, k) for dEy/dx\n        Ex_at_ijk_Hz = E[i, j, k, _EX]\n        Ex_at_ijp1k = E[i, j + 1, k, _EX]\n        Ey_at_ijk_Hz = E[i, j, k, _EY]\n        Ey_at_ip1jk = E[i + 1, j, k, _EY]\n\n        dEx_dy_Hz = (Ex_at_ijp1k - Ex_at_ijk_Hz) / dy\n        dEy_dx_Hz = (Ey_at_ip1jk - Ey_at_ijk_Hz) / dx\n\n        mu_Hz = mu_zz[i, j, k]\n        ch_Hz = -dt / (mu_Hz + 1e-20)\n        H[i, j, k, _HZ] += ch_Hz * (dEx_dy_Hz - dEy_dx_Hz)\n\n    # kernels\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    @wp.kernel\n    def pole_residue_electric_update_3d(\n        E: wp.array(dtype=wp.float32),\n
